name: Uke-Shogi
description: Uke-Shogi is a Japanese defensive card game inspired by Shogi (Japanese Chess) concepts. The 'Uke' (受け) refers to defense. Players use standard cards to represent chess-like pieces, focusing on defensive positioning and piece capture mechanics. A niche hybrid of card and board game concepts.

history.origins: Uke-Shogi (Imo Shogi, 芋将棋) was a Japanese card game popular in the late 19th and early 20th century. It was documented in 1927 under the name Imo Shogi in the judicial survey Tobaku ni kansuru chôsa (A Research into Gambling). The game used a deck of 40 or 42 cards representing Shogi pieces (Kings, Rooks, Bishops, Golds, Silvers, Knights, Lances, Pawns) and is considered a possible ancestor of Goita. Surviving descriptions are brief and ambiguous; the game is no longer played.
timeline: Late 19th–early 20th century: Popular in Japan; described in 1927 as Imo Shogi in Tobaku ni kansuru chôsa (A Research into Gambling).

setup.deck: Historical sources describe a dedicated shogi-piece card pack (around 40-42 cards), not a standard French 52-card deck.
setup.dealing: Cards dealt to represent board positions.

rules.objective: Be the first player to play all your cards (empty your hand) to win the deal. Players take turns matching the current lead card or passing; the last player to match plays a new card until one player runs out.
rules.gameplay: Cards represent Shogi pieces with specific movement rules. Focus on defensive (Uke) strategy. Captured cards can be redeployed (drop mechanic from Shogi). Promotion possible when reaching opponent's territory.

strategy.intermediate: Use captured cards for surprise drops.
